title: Why operating cash flow differs from net income this month
prompt: Explain why operating cash flow differs from net income this month using working capital and noncash movements.

setup.q: Which balance sheet accounts belong to each cash flow line (operating, investing, financing) when Dime's default mapping is not right?

inputs.name: Realtime statement of cash flows, balance sheet and profit and loss

steps: pull the profit and loss, the opening and closing balance sheets and Dime's statement of cash flows for the month
run scf_indirect with cashFlowMapping: net income, noncash items, working capital movements, operating cash flow
write the bridge from net income to operating cash flow with one line per movement and the driver behind each

done.text: Net income at the top of the bridge equals Dime's profit and loss for the period
Every exception row (a movement without a driver, a mapping gap) cites the account id
cash-vs-income-bridge.xlsx opens with Exceptions first (count and total on the first rows), a Tie-out block whose Difference is 0.00, and no internal plumbing words
The bridge lines sum to operating cash flow with no residual; each movement is explained in plain words
